name: fno_vs_cash_rotation_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Stocks in the F&O segment experience different intraday dynamics than cash-only stocks because F&O stocks attract leveraged speculative flow. On days when F&O stocks with high open interest (OI) buildup outperform, it signals leveraged speculation that tends to unwind intraday. Cash-only stocks, driven by delivery buyers, show more persistent moves. The strategy exploits this divergence: when F&O-active stocks spike due to futures-driven buying (visible via OI increase + price rise), fade the move expecting intraday profit-taking by leveraged traders. Simultaneously, when cash-only stocks show similar momentum, follow it as it's more likely delivery-driven and persistent. This inefficiency exists because most retail traders don't separate their analysis by F&O vs cash dynamics.
universe: NIFTY 200: split into F&O segment (~180 stocks) and cash-only (~20 stocks)
stock_filter: F&O stocks: ADV > ₹20 crore, daily OI data available. Cash-only: ADV > ₹10 crore

other: intraday OI change for F&O stocks

indicators.name: fno_momentum_bps
indicators.formula: median(return_30min) across top 10 F&O stocks by intraday OI increase

indicators.name: cash_momentum_bps
indicators.formula: median(return_30min) across top 10 cash-only stocks by 30-min return

conditions: OI_change_pct > 5 for F&O leader stocks (speculative buildup)
F&O leader stock close > VWAP (momentum still active)
long.confirmation: short the F&O leader (fade speculative spike); long the cash leader (follow delivery flow)

conditions: OI_change_pct decreasing for F&O laggard stocks (unwinding)
short.confirmation: long the F&O laggard (bounce from unwind); short the cash leader (fade after overshoot)

entry.entry_price: market order on both legs simultaneously

exit.trailing_stop: 5 bps trailing on each leg independently
exit.signal_exit: OI starts building in opposite direction (regime change)

risk.position_sizing: ₹50K per leg (F&O leg + cash leg), market-neutral

filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:00; allow first entry after 10:00
filters.volume_filter: F&O stock volume > 1.5x average (confirms speculative activity)
filters.trend_filter: prefer days when NIFTY 50 is range-bound (±0.5% intraday)
filters.event_filter: skip on monthly F&O expiry day (OI dynamics distorted by rollover)
other_filters: skip if fewer than 5 cash-only stocks have meaningful volume

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — the structural difference between leveraged F&O flow and delivery-based cash flow is permanent. Edge may narrow as more traders monitor OI data but will not disappear.

weaknesses: Cash-only stocks in NIFTY 200 are few (~20) and often illiquid. Executing meaningful positions without market impact is challenging.
Intraday OI data from NSE is delayed and noisy — real-time OI is approximated from option chain snapshots, not precise.
The premise that F&O flow is speculative and cash flow is delivery-driven is an oversimplification. Institutional F&O hedging activity creates non-speculative OI buildup.
prior_art: Ni, Pan & Poteshman (2008) 'Volatility Information Trading in the Option Market'. Easley, O'Hara & Srinivas (1998) 'Option Volume and Stock Prices'. In India, Srivastava et al. (2015) study F&O activity impact on underlying prices.
notes: SEBI's periodic reduction of F&O-eligible stocks means the cash-only universe is shrinking over time. If the cash-only segment becomes too small, the strategy may need to pivot to comparing high-OI vs low-OI within the F&O segment.
